data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The panel-versus-expert reliability comparison is empirically undecidable in a single evaluation because any observed superior accuracy of the panel can be attributed to either genuine reasoning or mere compliance, and these hypotheses make identical point predictions for aggregate accuracy; only the structure of errors can partially separate them, but even error structure is confounded by checklist quality.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the evaluation includes held-out cases deliberately constructed to probe known checklist blind spots, error structure becomes diagnostic and the two hypotheses can be separated.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the panel's error pattern is random even on cases outside the checklist's coverage, this is evidence of genuine reasoning beyond mere compliance and the undecidability claim fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert's errors are also structured (by systematic bias), then comparing error structures between panel and expert can distinguish genuine reliability from both compliance and expert bias.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a within-evaluation proxy for reasoning\u2014such as member-level justification transcripts coded for rule-recitation versus independent reasoning\u2014correlates with decorrelated error patterns, the single evaluation gains discriminative power.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In a single evaluation, both 'genuine reliability gain' and 'mere compliance that tracks the right answer' predict that the panel will match or beat the expert on verifiable outcomes. The distinction only becomes empirically tractable if we observe error patterns: compliance predicts structured errors aligned with checklist blind spots, genuine reasoning predicts dispersed errors. But this separation itself depends on the checklist having identifiable, observable blind spots. If the checklist's blind spots are unknown or if it happens to cover the test distribution perfectly, the two hypotheses are observationally equivalent within that evaluation.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
